Bucky feels her body reform, shaping itself to the surrounding walls. Memories of the last week begin to flood through her, acting as a glue to keep the disparate pieces of her whole. From the convoy, to Paradise, to the bowels of the church. She remembers all of what happened, more or less. Eventually, she remembers remembering. Then, she catches up to the present.

Bucky wakes up in the middle of Paradise. She sits on the road, in front of a building she never paid any mind to. A sign denotes it as the residence and workplace of the local cobbler. It is impossible to know if she will enter into this building. The ground beneath her shakes with a fury, and a shadow grows overhead. At the end of town, she can see the church ascending, higher and higher into the sky. It stays connected to the ground, unearthing more of the ruins beneath every second.
I blink my eyes rapidly, trying to get a grip. On anything, really. A grasp, maybe? I don't exactly- I look up to see what's causing the shadow to be cast on Paradise.
The shadow is cast from the church, growing ever higher. It almost seems as if it will break through the sky.
How quickly are we talking? A few inches a minute?
It's hard to say from this distance, but it'd be closer to several feet every minute.
Ah.

Well. It would be pretty bad if that fell over, haha! I mean, what am I going to do about it, right? Although- apparently I can survive a direct stab wound to the chest, so I would probably be fine no matter what. Right? I'm immortal now? Or delusional, or dreaming, or the magic that brought me back was one-time-use only, or at the behest of someone manipulating me, or only temporary and I'll die again once I fulfil my purpose, or if I try too hard to fulfil my purpose, or if I make the wrong move in general, or say the wrong thing. But who knows what the wrong thing is, right? Who would tell me that? Probably someone, I'm sure.
I go check to see if it's the local cobbler.

The cobbler's place of work isn't particularly large. Shoes line the shelves, and there seem to be some repairs being performed to a few. The cobbler sits behind the desk, hammering a nail into one. Behind him is a door to a back room.
"Hi! Are you the cobbler?"
He looks up from his work. "That'd be me. Got a shoe problem?"
"Yeah, maybe. What counts as a shoe? Is life a shoe? I'm sure you've got some opinion on that."
"There's a building growing outside, you know. I'm sure lots of people with shoes are inside it, or maybe just nearby."
"Well, it's first come, first served here. Gotta finish these repairs. I'm sure all that can wait."
"Why are you sure of that?"
"What makes you so confident you don't have any part to play in helping people?"
"Aren't I helping people now? I mean, if some disaster came, I'd drop everything, sure. But shoe's aren't the end of the world. Might be a bit uncomfortable, is all."

"This is a disaster! Everything's a fucking disaster! It's been disaster after disaster since I got here, as far as I'm concerned! Maybe if shoes aren't the end of the world, you should actuall try and do something about the end of the world, eh?"
"Oh, whatever."
"Look, do you know why I'm alive?"
"Well, I could give you the scoop on the birds and the bees, but I got a feeling that's not what you mean." He sets down his hammer and shoe. "Were you attacked? Is someone after you?"
"Okay, sure." I head into the back room. There has to be a reason why I was dropped here, of all places.

...He's seated at a table, polishing a shoe, oblivious to the world around him. His back is turned, so he doesn't even seem to notice her enter. Michael "Ellie 'Ace' Tither" Acilis is in the cobbler's back room.
"You."
His head turns. When his eyes fall on her, he almost falls out of his chair in surprise. "M-Mari! Where have you been!?"
"Hanging out with Voreverl. Then dead." I walk over slowly and sit down across from him.
"Dead!?" He doesn't seem to know how to process that.
"Yeah, I got stabbed by a vine. How have you been?"
"Well... Just been, um, waiting for you, I guess?" He sets down the shoe. "I got this job. Just... in training right now, but it's nice."
"Yeah? How's the... girl thing going?"

He looks very uncomfortable, all of a sudden. "It... doesn't have to be going. I was, um, in a pretty bad spot... S-so it was probably just... manipulation, I guess. Virchow must've just... messed with my head. Made me think you could... like me, even if I was... like that."
"Oh, no, I doubt it. People can't really be knocked off course that easily. It takes a long time to build up the willpower to contravene what the world decided for you."
"I was annoyed at you for a long time for being so easy. But I think that's probably not giving you enough credit. You did this to yourself. Right?"
"Virchow's off doing something else, he left you here on your own, and I bet you still want to be a girl."
"..." He can't bear to look her in the eye anymore. "...Why do I have to be so selfish...?"

I sigh. "Yeah, I dunno. I guess it's easy to fall into that kind of trap. You think you're revealing some big secret truth about how things were meant to be, how things were supposed to go, and it's just a coincidence that it's what you wanted anyways."
"I don't think I can help you, Ace. But that's probably fine. You'll probably be fine."
"I couldn't help much of anyone, at the end of the day."

I put my elbows on the table and my chin in my hands, slouching forward. "We should probably get out of here, right? Did you see the big tower out there? Might be my fault, honestly. In some weird way."
"I tried too hard when it didn't matter, then didn't try hard enough the one time I knew it did."

"I mean, I did tell them to stop. I was a little bit persistent about it. Could've actually insisted on something, put myself out there, but I figured I had already tried that approach plenty of times, so, it probably..."

"...You're just giving up...? You're just going to... run away?" He looks at her. There's something else in his expression now. It's hard to place at first, but it almost looks like he's disgusted with the thing sitting across from him.

"Being okay with something isn't the same as giving up on it. You're not giving up on the gender thing, right? I'm telling you I'm okay with that. I accept it. You, Ace, are a girl. You're still my friend. We can still hug if you want. I can still call you Cilly. We can still run around together, you can still be weirdly nervous about everything, whatever. Those were the main things I liked doing, to be honest."
"There'll be a dark spot somewhere on the map, but we can navigate around it."
"Isn't that what you want?"

"How could you..." He slams his fist on the table, and stans up with a jolt. "How could you think *that's* what I want!? That I want everything to just be... that I want us to just... ignore this!? Like it doesn't change anything!? Just go back to normal life!? I don't *want* a normal life! I don't want *you* to want a normal life! I don't want you to give up, I want you to save this town! I want you to stop at nothing! I want you to be fearless! I want your ideals to mean something! A-and I want you to drag me along, even when I'm hesitant, even when I mess up! And, and..."

He's crying. Snot's dripping from his nose. He can't hold himself together anymore. "I don't want you to just be okay with me being like this... I want you to *want* it. I want you to show me the way. You're my hero, and... you're a real girl! You've always been one! So... I want you to tell me what to do! Show me how to be like you! You have to! You have to save me! Please! Please, Mari... save me..."

I lower my head fully onto the table, maybe hoping that he slams it again and gives me a concussion. "My ideals, Mike? My ideals were that I wanted a normal life. I wanted people to be happy, I wanted them to be okay, I wanted things to be the way they were supposed to be. Everything I wanted besides that wasn't an ideal, it was just more selfishness. And you can't tell me to do both at once. You have to choose. Do you want me to want a weird, fucked up existence, where my best friend is a freak, and the church destroys everyone's lives, and the government gets away with everything, or do you want my ideals to mean something? Because... I'm fine with them not meaning this... I'm fine with it... it's okay if my ideals don't mean I have to give everything up. I don't know why you want me to give everything up. I don't get it. I'm telling you that I want to spend time with you. I'm telling you that I want you around. I'm telling you exactly what you're making me tell you. You can't be unhappy with it. It's not fair. It's not fair."

"Mari..." He doesn't slam the table, instead opting to just awkwardly stand there. "I *am* a freak. I've just... gotten worse at hiding it. That's not going to change just because we pretend to live a normal life. The church isn't gonna stop, and neither is the government. More towns will get wiped off the map. People displaced, sold into slavery. You wanted to stop that... how is *that* selfish?"
"Yeah."
I don't move.
Maybe he'll be forced to force me to do something.
Or maybe not.

The sound of a door slamming comes from the front room.

First, the cobbler's voice. "Hello. Got a shoe problem?"

Then... "BUUCCCKKKKSSSS! YOU IN HERE!?"
Ace's eye twitches. "Really...? A call to adventure, and you're rejecting it? You're *really* going to just... sit there?"
"If it's so easy to reject a call to adventure, it's not a very good call, is it?" I mumble.
She'll probably be in the room in a minute.

"That... is... it!" Ace grabs Bucky's wrist. "Just this once, okay!? Just this once, I'm gonna save you! Because just this once... I know for sure. I know that *I'm* right, and *you're* wrong!" He attempts to drag her out of the back room.

He's so weak. Not a single muscle in that girl. There's no way he could ever actually drag me anywhere if I gave a shit about staying. Pathetic. But... I don't know. The effort is charming. I feel a bit charmed. This is what I was asking for a second ago, right? Forcefulness? A tiny, imperceptible smile comes to my face, and I stumble to my feet, following him out.

Voreverl is wearing an ostentatious outfit. She has a red top hat and jacket. In her gloved hand is a cane, though it's clearly for show. There's no mask covering her face, so her bright green eyes and pointy ears are set free to the world.

It looks like she was about to leave, but her ears perk up at the sound of Ace and Mari shambling into the front room. She turns to face them with a grin. "Finally! Been going door to door since I got outta there!"
"Heyyy. What's up, evil queen?"
"Got an exciting quest for us, right? That's what my buddy here is telling me, anyways."

"Gweheheh. Oh, I'm just here to ask for a favor. You see, a while ago, I funded this silly old steam locomotive. And now?" She mimics an explosion with her hands. "I'm thinking I need it gone. Whaddaya say?"

Atie's life travels through her body. Her physical form reshapes, molding to its new container. As it does the last week plays in her mind, acting as an attractive force between the particles known as her. It was only interrupted once, as Penny attempted to remove her mind, compromising the integrity of the memories. Ultimately, Atie chose to return to her own body, regardless of consequences. Of course, this had all already happened. The replay reaches its end. We're caught up to the present.

Atie wakes up, lying in the desert sand, next to a set of rails. The train sits upon them, looming over her. She's back at the station. In the distance, over a hill, something is rising. The church ascends to the clouds.
Atie slowly gets up, coughing as the sand all around covers her, and trying to brush it off.
The sand is brushed off successfully. Somehow, though, it feels like she'll never be free of it all.
She checks her watch.
It's working normally. The time seems accurate, too. It's almost sunset.
She goes to the train in search of anyone else.

She comes across three people in the lounge car. Rhea sits, facing a wall, bearing a distant expression. Val is seated on the opposite side of the car, resting her head against a fist, looking annoyed. Bixbite stands between the two of them, looking back and forth in thought.

[Do they know too...?]
"Hi..."

Val and Rhea ignore her.

Only Bixbite acknowledges her entrance. "Alcule, right? What is it you do around here?"
"I... was... assistant to the engineer." Atie points to Rhea.

Bixbite considers this. "That could work. Only in a pinch, though. It would be better to have everyone on board. We only get one shot at this. My liege has been waiting for this day for so long, and it's been so boring."
"What are you talking about?"
"How caught up are you? Do you know about the monster? The one that's waking up?"
"The one they called Thromb?"

"I've never been good with names. Point is, it's been slumbering under this town longer than the founding of any nation still around. It's about to burst from the ground, and then it's gonna bring destruction and ruin. Sounds like my kinda party, but we've got a better idea."
"Didn't he burst a moment ago? Or is... ugh... this is so confusing..."

"Something already happened underground. There's been occasional quakes for a bit now. Lucky for us, that thing was buried deep. We've still got time until it reaches the surface. When it does, we need something that can deal with it."
"I still don't know how we ended up back here, but... what are you thinking of?"

"Why do you think we funded this in the first place?" She gestures at the walls of the train car. "We're gonna lure it over here, and ram the whole thing right into it. Of course, we'll need a crew to operate it. That's where you come in."
"And we survive...?"
"Sure. Just jump out at the last second. Soft landings around here."
"Why me, then? Why not Rhea?"
Bixbite motions to Rhea, silently staring at the wall. "She's been unresponsive like that ever since I found her. I don't care who operates this thing, so if you can snap her out of it, go ahead."

Atie is deeply unsure. 
"...Rhea?"

Rhea doesn't move.

"Good luck with that." Bixbite shrugs, and moves to the exit. Before leaving, she seems to remember something, and turns to Atie with a sadistic grin. "Oh, and one more thing."

"I'm gonna need you to re-enable that 'explosion button' you two turned off. Just ramming it might not be good enough to finish it off. Plus, this way we get to watch a real bloodbath." She licks her lips, beginning to salivate, then ducks out of the car.

Like a song played in an echo chamber, Briar's memories of her life reverberate back onto herself. She feels herself shifting, becoming one with the shape of this crevice. All the while, the story of her life begins to play in her mind. This past week in great, though perhaps not entirely accurate, detail. Even some days years before. A concert, a story, the birth of a cursed child. Then, the present.

She wakes up on the streets of Paradise, near the town square. She's facing a familiar building. It's the Narita Inn. She only paid for four nights; her stay here should be complete. Somehow, it doesn't seem as if this town will reach another night. The ground shakes, and on the edge of town, she can see it: The church rises towards the clouds, unburying itself from the desert sand. It rises higher and higher, as if in insult to the sky itself.
Slowly she stands up looking around confused. Briar walks towards the inn looking for any familiar face.

Upon entering the inn, she spots the old innkeeper seated behind the desk, as always. He's writing something in a note book, but looks up from it as she enters.

"Ah, welcome back. Sorry, but... given how this looks to be the end of the world, we ain't exactly open for business tonight. You're free to wait it out here, if'n you want."
"What... what happened? Where is Kit? Alonsa? Thromb..?" she approaches him
"Takin' a guess here that you were at the heart of whatever exactly happened. Must've shaken you up somethin' fierce. It's alright if you need a minute."
"I was... deep underground. Is it just you here?"

"...Mayor's daughter is upstairs. Saavedra found her in the sheriff's office, 'longside..." There's a sad look in his eyes. "...Well, not that it matters now. Didn't seem right to take her home, for some reason, so I gave her a room on the house."
"Nene! Is she okay? Can I go see her?"

"Don't see why not. I'll show you to her room." He closes his book as he stands, and leads Briar to a room on the second floor. As he walks, he keeps the conversation going. "How'd you two get acquainted? Kid's always locked up, ain't she?"
"I- Cory took me to meet her... she repaired my violin"

"That's mighty kind of her." Once they reach the door to the room, the innkeeper knocks on it. "Alright if we come in?"

There's no response.
"Nene, it's me Briar. Is it okay if I see you?"

Still no response. The innkeeper is starting to look worried. He deliberates for a moment, before deciding to open the door.

The room's empty. The window's open. All of the sheets have been removed from the bed, tied into a rope, and thrown out the window to be climbed down from.
Briar quickly runs inside towards the window, looking down
The rope of bedsheets extends almost all the way to the ground. It's not the safest way down, but it's functional. There's no sight of Nene from the window.
"I- I need to go look for her" she quickly storms out of the inn

"We can cover more ground with the both of us." The innkeeper follows behind her. However, they find the path out of the inn blocked. Tae Narita, the bartender, stands at the entrance to the building. She faces them with a vacant stare, and an empty smile.
"Narita excuse me, I really need to pass by" Briar says trying to look around her for a gap to run through{

The door is shut tightly behind her. She'd have to be moved out of the way. Tae looks exasperated at Briar's words. "That's it, then? How irresponsible, yes, how irresponsible indeed. You wish to leave, now, after you have destroyed our peace? I know it was your kind. Our invaders. You released the slumbering beast, didn't you?"
"Narita it isn't time for this, I need to go look for Nene, please"

"What's the point in that?" Tae raises her hands as if to gesture, but doesn't know what to do with them. "It's over, haven't you seen? Haven't you felt it? This town, its long history, every one of its inhabitants... I kept it running for so long. You destroyed it within a week. Are you proud of yourself?"
"I didn't destroy it, I don't want this town to be destroyed either! And I don't care if the world is ending, I can't let Nene be by herself during it"

"...Why? What's the point of that?" She places a hand to her forehead, her smile fading. "The others weren't aware. They forgot. It faded, drawn over again and again. But I couldn't forget. Every life I've lived in this town, again and again. I could never forget. But now... it will be sent back to nothing. Nothing we do from this point on will change that."
"Every life...? What do you mean Narita?" she tilts her head

"You don't know... You don't even know..." She sounds amused, but her face displays nothing. "This town has existed for so long, with the same people... Our bodies were not immortal, so our lives were restarted regularly. The others... their memories blurred of each previous life. Of each cycle. Some could go on living, as if nothing had happened. Others... the sheriff, the mayor... they knew something was wrong. That they were trapped in some inescapable maelstrom. They realized the futility of escape, but did not know why. I, on the other hand... I was so thankful. The town I loved would go on forever. Our reverie would not need to come to an end."
"How? When you die you just come back?"
"Will it be the same this time or how- how does it work? I still need to go look for her"

"We're regrown in the ground, like seeds fallen from a tree. This whole town... I'm sure of it, we're all just that priest's garden. Well, we were." Color is fading from her face. "It won't be the same this time. That terrible beast... after all I did to it, I know what it's come here to do. It will rip us out by the roots. It will salt the earth. Nothing will grow here again. So I ask you again... what is the point?"
"Maybe we can prevent it, a hero always saves the day! And if we can't... no one should die alone that's why" Briar walks closer to Narita

"Why?" She doesn't raise her voice, but it sounds more forceful. "Why would that matter? Our final moments have no meaning. We won't remember. No one will."

"...Then why did you come here?" The old man finally speaks to his daughter. Her eyes widen at his words, but she doesn't respond.

Briar gets closer extending her arms slightly "Because no one deserves to be alone during their last breath. Your last breath in this world shouldn't be one filled with loneliness, death is scary enough already."

She grabs Briar's arms, keeping them away from her. "You are a hypocrite. You are empty, and you stand for nothing. You see fear as the enemy? Fear of loneliness, and of death? Yet... you would not shed that fear. When you were placed in my game... you forfeited the match. Scared, and pathetic, you ran. You could have won. You are strong. Why did you not embrace the joy of victory, and superiority. You hate fear... yet you embrace it."

"I'm always scared... I let fear take over me more often than not. I will never be close to be courageous like the heroes in book. I didn't want to hurt anyone that's why I ran" Briar starts sniffling "I don't want to feel superior to anyone, I just want to be equals. And- if the world ends, I know I wouldn't want to be alone because that's scarier than death could ever be"

"You're wrong. You're just afraid to take it into your hands. To let it flow through you. When you inflict pain, you understand the truth. As long as you are strong, nothing can hurt you. That is true joy. Tell me how it felt. Tell me what went through you... when you killed that man. What did you feel?" She brings her face closer to Briar. Something is buried deep in her otherwise empty expression. A tiny, pinprick point of desperation.

"I-" tears fall down her face "I regret it every second I breathe, I just wanted to protect Bucky I didn't want them to her, I tell myself I had no choice but that doesn't get rid of his face from my mind... I feel like a monster. I never felt joy, I just try to forget I did such a thing"

"Oh... then... did anyone enjoy my games...?" The desperation is replaced with something else. She falls to her knees. "Hurting my servant... it made him so sad. I did not want to rule through fear. I wanted my subjects to feel happy. So I left it to them... I put the power to inflict pain in their hands."

"...I'm betting they were just too afraid to tell you how those games made 'em feel. Only a monster wouldn't feel fear 'bout having to hurt others. Even you..." The Old Man leans down, placing a hand on her shoulder. "...That boy, you hated hurting him. It made you so afraid of yourself. Still, you coveted the control it gave you. You found a way to remove yourself, to hurt them, while you didn't have to lift a finger. That's when you lost touch with your humanity."
Briar dries off her face with her hands "I need to go look for Nene I'm sorry, please keep her company"

The Old Man nods, helping Tae move out of the way of the door.

Before Briar can leave, Tae speaks in a defeated voice. "Wait... I saw her. On my way here, I saw Nene Shishido. I asked her where she was going. I can tell you where to look, but... there is something you need to know."
"Tell me, what is it?"

"She was on her way to the mayor's mansion. But... her exact words. She said she was going home to speak to her father." She looks up at Briar, with an expression of sympathy. "Be careful, Briar McGregor."

Alonsa's body softens, shifting into the shape of her container. The gaps left by her wounds fill in, and her skin presses against the sandstone walls. As her shape morphs, her mind begins to melt alongside it. To keep herself together, she automatically cycles through the memories of her past.

As if guided by an unseen force, a voyeuristic cage conveying the world to her, she makes her way through the memories of the past week. Alongside it, she sees... something else. The memories of a figure long past. Are either of these truly accurate? Is this what happened, at either time? Does she recall the shape she's always had, or can see only see herself as what she has become?

Was this truly destiny, predetermined by fate... or was it a memory of what had already happened?
Alonsa wakes up on a cold sandstone floor, somewhere within the halls of the church. There's voices further down the hall, but she can't quite make them out from here.
She shoots up in a cold sweat, and starts panting heavily.
She feels her head, where the incision was made.
There is no wound, or even scar, to be found.
"I'm... this isn't..."
"I must be dead..."
"Then, is this the afterlife?"
It doesn't much feel like it.
Alonsa gets up.
Alonsa finds herself able to stand.
She heads toward the sounds

Theo McGregor is slumped over against a wall. Several severe bruises are visible on his face.

Tanner is standing over him with a furious expression. "You bastard! Stop dodging the question! What the bell is going to happen now!?"
Alonsa approaches them.
"Tanner?"
"You're... what's going on?"

"A-Alonsa!" Tanner looks shocked to see her. "It... it worked? I... I can't believe it..."

"Then... sis is also..." Theo mutters to himself.
"What happened?"
"Last I remember..."
"I think my head exploded?"

"Y-yes... it was a grisly sight. I was stunned, unable to move, but... that traveler, Chara, or... the Dark Lord, I suppose. They told us to place the injured in those casts... to use them to heal you. I... I honestly thought you were too far gone. I didn't expect to... to ever see you again." He has difficulty getting through the explanation.
"...What?"
"The casts are what saved me?"
"I don't... that doesn't make any sense..."
"...W-well... what other explanation can there be? You're here now, aren't you?" There's a desperation to Tanner's voice, as if he's pleading with himself to believe his own words.
"No, I mean..."
"They were created... from someone else. They look like me, but... They aren't..."
"I don't know. I don't know!"

"...You look different." Theo speaks up. "I barely knew you, and even I can tell. They said this would happen. It's... still clearly you. But... the shape is all wrong. That's not the only thing he isn't telling you."

"Shut up! She... she just nearly died! She doesn't need this! Stop messing with our heads!" Tanner snaps at him.
"What do you mean...?"
"What do I..."
"A mirror. I need a mirror."
"Or... something. Anything. I need to see myself."
Theo reaches over for a violin, laying near him. With a simple strum, a piece of the sandstone wall turns into a mirror.
Alonsa looks at herself.
Her appearance is exactly as she remembers it.
"It looks... the same."
Alonsa looks closer.

No matter how hard she looks, it matches her memories perfectly.

"Your memories are probably... adapted. This is how you are now, so when you were healing... you forgot what you really looked like before. I'm sorry. I don't know what to say." Tanner looks away from her in shame.
"That... probably explains what happened then."
"I did die when he carved a hole in my head. And, whatever I am now, isn't the same as before."
Alonsa studies their features. They try to identify anything different, though they know its a hopeless task.
"What is different, anyway?"

"Well, well. Would you look at that? She figured it out on her own." Theo tries to get to his feet, but stumbles and falls against the wall again. "Life cannot come from death. Nothing in this world can revive the dead."

"..." Tanner tries to ignore Theo. "...Y-your, um, nose. J-just a lot of... bone structure, stuff, really. Th-the height's about... the same..."
"I always liked my height, anyway. Or... I think I always did."
"The thing that scares me about this... isn't even the change. I can deal with that. I can go on living. If we even make it out of this town..."
"I don't know if any records of the old me exist anymore, that's the thing. Maybe family portraits or something, from a decade ago."
"But nothing on who I am... Or, who I was, I suppose."
"It's alright, I suppose. What matters is what we have now. I'm alive! That's good, at least."
"Or, someone is alive, at the very least."

"Is that so...?" Theo rolls his head to the side, despondent. He chuckles under his breath, as if he doesn't know how else to react. "You don't understand... you don't understand a thing!"

"Will you just shut up!?" Tanner turns to him in anger. "This is all your fault, anyway! I know this was all just... part of your plan! What's next in your sick scheme!?"

Theo laughs harder. "My... my plan? Not a single thing has gone according to my plan. Do you think I would have turned my sister into a walking corpse if I had any other choice?"
"What even was your plan, anyway?" Alonsa doesn't stop looking at the mirror.

"..." Theo turns to look at her. "Once we'd assassinated the Yondovan Emperor, it would act as an excuse to seize control of the town. I'm on friendly terms with the next in line, they would've approved my proposal. Then... I'd have as much time to study the casts as I needed. I could've made a perfect world, where we could take on as much suffering as we needed to. For the sake of my sister."
"And, in your head, what did the casts do?"

"Seems I was more or less on the money. Rewriting of memories, desires, personality... With Yondova's musical industry, we could've had an assembly line, remaking an entire population." Theo smiles to himself. "Of course, I should've realized. When you build a railroad in a desert, you have to account for the shifting sands."

"...You're sick." Tanner looks disgusted with him.
"Was never going to work, anyway..."
"The past has a way of sticking to us."

"...Truer words may never have been spoken." Theo turns to Tanner. "And... I'm sorry. About your sister. I thought inviting her into my plans would be what was best. She was like me... all she wanted was to alleviate your burden. For that, she would've done anything. She's the real inventor of the steam locomotive. She was the brains behind deciphering the function of the casts. None of this would have been possible without her. She's a genius."

Tanner doesn't seem to know what to say to that. He has no idea where to direct the anger swelling inside of him.
She's still kind of a chef, in Alonsas head.
"I'm sure she can find a way to use her talents in the future."
"If we can get out of here..."

Tanner slowly nods at Alonsa's words. "Yes... I can't forgive you, Theo McGregor, but... I'm going to focus on the future. This time, I'll be alongside my sister. I'll help her find a better path. Just... stay out of our way."

"After the beating she gave me? Hah... I'd have to be crazy to go near her." Theo tries to stand up again, succeeding this time, propping himself up against the wall.
"What happened while I was out?"

"Honestly, not much." Tanner begins to explain. "We placed you, and the other injured, in the casts. Then, the... well, stuff that was happening... it seemed to trigger a cave-in. "I... had a bit of difficulty on the way." Theo joins in the recap. "To tell you the truth, it burns even standing right now. This has been a rough week on my body."
"What I mean is more... what happened to Thromb?"
"Where did he go?"

"Well, I'm exactly sure what-" As Tanner tries to answer, the ground shakes. Hard. The three of them fall to the ground. No, that's not right. They fall... to the wall. Gravity seems to shift, shoving them against the side of the hall. Of course, it's not gravity itself that has fallen. This church has been burrowing itself out of the ground, ever since its prisoner was freed from its cage. All that this tower has left to do... is fall.
"Right on cue, I guess..."
"We need to get out of here."
Alonsa looks around for where they can go.

She shouldn't worry. That will be much easier than she imagines.

The sandstone walls seem to melt away as she presses against them. Their composition changes from stone, to flesh, to wood, and then... just sand. No longer able to support her weight, it collapses. Through wall after wall she falls, as they seem to disintegrate into fine grains before she can reach them.

Finally, she reaches open air, and falls from the skies above Paradise. Above her, the church follows close behind, primed to crush everything beneath.

The beast that lies beneath the stone tower has awoken. His tendrils spread like an infection through its walls. It becomes one with him. A singular entity made with the single purpose of hatred and destruction. Upwards he drags the stones. Further, further. Past the rough sands that weigh him down. Higher, higher. Cracking the bedrock holding him in place. Just a little further.

First, just the highest floor breaks through the surface. Then, the second, third, fourth, and so on... The shadow cast over the town grows and grows. The church returns to its former glory. A towering monstrosity built to house sin itself. Then, when it can't lift any higher, its base begins to crumble. The pressure, the need to go even further, is too much for this rigid structure.

The lowest floor collapses, sending the tower hurtling to the ground. Before it can crush the town beneath, the cracks begin to spread. Pulled taut by his roots, the entire building begins to break apart. What an inflexible material. It is no problem for one such as him. This is no longer a cage. This has become the beast's skin.

A song begins to play. Flowing over the town like the waves of a tsunami. His hatred curdles into a melody. The notes of rage transform him into a form more suited to the destruction he wishes to sow. The sandstone tower transforms. Some of its bricks turn to flesh; they weave together in a bloated, blistered mess. Others to wood; their gnarled, rotten branches splintering and twisting around the pulsating tissue. Some simply fall apart into grains of sand; gaping holes left in the structure as its very framework begins to disintegrate and reform in a cycle.

The mass collapses upon its own weight. Unfocused. Unbalanced. Its rage makes it as blind as it is incomprehensible. It needs a guiding hand. A mind to center its rage. I have had so long to think. So long to consider how to destroy all of you. Wouldn't it be best to keep it simple? To crush you within the palm of my hand. To taste your blood burst from your body. That is what I wish for, and the flesh responds in turn.

A ribcage bursts forth from beneath the shifting skin, a spinal cord anchoring it together. It contains the mass, gives it shape. Then, two skeletal arms break free. The wooden, sandy, stony flesh begins to crawl across the bones, giving them the illusion of muscles and ligaments. They can't hold solid form, continuing to fall apart and reform into different materials, but it does not matter. It can drag itself across the sand with sheer force of will.

Finally, a skull emerges. It dwarfs even the largest buildings in the town. The flesh is already spread thin across the ribs and arms. Tendrils of this uneven composition crawl onto the skull enough to keep it steady, but they're unable to completely fill it. Its eye sockets are left empty, unable to convey the spiraling chaos that has been set free. The wild, untamed nature at the heart of human hatred.

It reaches out its hand, the skeletal structure still visible as the sands and flesh continue to melt off of it. Then, all at once, the arm slams down across the town. Anything in its path is crushed, pulverized into nothing. It grips the ground, and begins to drag itself forward, towards the mansion seated opposite from it. Everything in between will be ground into dust. There are other matters to attend to, of course, but the death of this forsaken town will be the first victory that this monster tastes.

The roof collapses as a tremendous force crashes through it. The cobbler's place of work is left half-crushed by the side of a skeletal arm, flesh-like substances clinging to its surface. The cobbler is crushed beneath, flattened by the oversized limb. The other three are thrown against the remaining wall by a burst of wind, generated by the monstrous creature's attack. A sweltering wave of heat washes over them, radiating from its surface.

"Oomph!" I slam against the bricks, all the air getting knocked out of my lungs before I crash down to the ground. As I lay there, slowly regaining my senses, I roll over to look up at whatever it is that just attacked us.
"Wh-what the... what the fuck?"
"Is this yours, Voreverl?!"
"I could have figured out a way to destroy the train without... without killing some random guy!!"
I prop myself up on my elbows.

"Why did it explode the roof *right* when you did that explosion thing? Don't you think that's a bit too much of a coincidence?"

The arm begins to lift itself, revealing the ground beneath it. Everything beneath isn't simply crushed, but also seems to be melting from the overwhelming heat. It clings to the surface of the flesh, slowly sinking into it.

Ace follows behind the two of them. Once they're out of the building, the owner of the arm becomes visible. Its massive skeletal torso and head can be seen at the end of town, as its arms drag itself across the rows of buildings.

"Gw-gweh... I thought I saw... it was just for a moment, but... that guy, the store owner... in the arm, just under the surface... it looked like his face... like it was still alive." She shakes her head and starts running, perpendicular to the monster's path.

"What?! So, it's absorbing the townspeople?? That's sick! That's absolutely sick! I'm running next to them.

"That doesn't really explain why they would still be alive."
"Isn't being reduced to a puddle of goo a bit more chaotic than not?"
"...I just don't think anything in this town knows how to die anymore." She glances at Bucky for a moment before turning away. "It's not important. The plan stays the same."
"Wait, are we immortal?"
"I mean, I know you are."
"Is that actually how I survived getting stabbed? I thought I was going crazy..."

"Stop calling him that. It's gross."
I feel around my chest for a stab wound.

There's no wound, not even a scar.

I doubt Voreverl had to do much to convince her. But it still feels wrong.
"You know, I talked to her one time about how mad she was that she couldn't change anything about herself."
"Makes the whole thing kind of ironic, doesn't it?"
I curl my nose at the rotting flesh and turn away from it. "You didn't really need to show me that again to make your point, though."
"Sorry, what are we doing with this? Explain."

"...Sorry about that, I don't get a lotta chances for visual storytelling." She zips up the bag. "Her inability to change is exactly why we need her. "So, what, we did all this just for a bomb? You couldn't just build one the normal way?"
"Is that outside the great power of the emperor?"
"Used one minion to kill two stones, so sue me. Besides..." She lifts up one side of the body bag. "No, I couldn't make a bomb. Not one like this, anyway. Trust me, you're in for a bell of a show."
"I doubt she would've wanted any more shows. But, you know what? I think she'd be happy getting to blow up something that deserves it for once. No need to sugarcoat things." I give a slight smile.
"Fine. Let's do it."
"I want to get rid of that fucking train."

"Gweheheh, can't wait to knock down one of my toys, huh? Come on, grab the other end." Voreverl motions to the other side of the body bag. Ace is also present, and could be asked to help lift it, but Voreverl doesn't entertain this notion.
I take hold of it.

She leads them back out the building. The monstrous creature, still dragging itself by the arms, has almost reached this building. They're right on the edge of town, so they might be able to get out of its way if they move fast.
"So, uh, which direction is this thing in?"
"Hold on tight!" Gripping her side of the body, Voreverl does her best to run while carrying it. Ace follows closely, not sure if he should be doing something.
"Wah!" I stumble after her. "A little help, Ace?!"

"R-right!" Ace grabs hold, alleviating some of the weight burdening Bucky. A massive ribcage rolls over the town behind them, just barely missing them. A second later and it would've grazed their bodies, beginning the melting process. They're so close, the heat is almost unbearable.
"Agh! Faster, guys!"

"Hold your tongue! Voreverl Leocot decides her own pace, which I've decided will be increasing now!" Voreverl speeds up. Ace follows suit, too shocked by the near death experience to speak.

The ribcage continues grinding along the ground behind them, but not towards them. It's heading somewhere else. As long as it doesn't change its course, it won't be a danger, for the moment.
I breathe a sigh of relief. "Okay, okay, we can probably slow down now, don't want to wear ourselves out too early in the trek."
"If that's what Voreverl Leocot decides, of course."

"Hmm... I find it acceptable." She slows down, and looks back to Bucky. "Train's not far, just over those hills, you two hanging in there?"

Ace slows down in turn, continuing to try to match the speed of the group. "Um... Y-yeah, I think I'm good. Looks like the whole town's gonna be crushed if we stop to rest, so..."
"Yeah, he's doing fine. So, how does this fuse thing work?"
"Also, are you SURE Bixbite is competent enough to set it up?"

"Gwehah! Don't worry, Bixxy was just supposed to find the engineers and convey the message. We've got some smart cookies, from what I've heard. Only the best serving my empire." I say this with a weird hint of excitement in my voice. I'm interested in how she pulled this all off, as disturbing as it might be. Is it wrong for me to feel that way?

"Safeguards? In a project *I'm* funding? You've gotta start lowering you expectations here." She rolls her eyes. "They'll go along with it because if they don't, we're all gonna die. Not everything's a big evil conspiracy, Bucks."

"Okay, but won't *they* think it's a big evil conspiracy? An untraceable message from the emperor demanding that they destroy the emperor's project for no reason? I would doubt it, if it was on my head..."
"You're so negative. It's gonna work because it's my genius plan, and my genius plans always work. The universe is fond of me, didn't you know?"
"You know what, yeah, that's a good point. It sure does seem to be."
"Fine! Let's get this thing done! No more bitching from me!"
"You know, maybe you could've accused me of doing this whole thing as an excuse to get away from home, but dammit, I'm not home right now, and I still want to do it. So, that's gotta say something."
"Right, Ace?"

"..." Voreverl shoots him a side glance. "Maybe I should have *some* safeguards in my hiring process."
Several thunderous crashing sounds ring out from outside the train. They sound distant, in the direction of the town.
"No way..."

Val takes in a long breath, leading to a vaguely frustrated exhale. She stands up and faces Atie. "So, what are we gonna do? Personally, I'm all for ramming this thing into whatever that is outside. Just get rid of this thing so we can all move on."

"..." Val looks conflicted, debating whether to respond to her mother.
Atie chuckles, and starts walking towards the engine room.

Before entering, Atie pauses. She reaches into her right pocket and takes out a decent, adjustable, but comically short wrench. Inside, Atie begins to unscrew a lone bolt located to the side of the engine, accompanied only by a handle. The whole experience gives her a thought, although it's just a guess. "Do you normally help her with this?"

"I see."

Atie crawls out carefully, wanting to finish the operation before explaining.

Alonsa continues to fall through the air, as the tower in front of her ceases its threat to crush her. Before her very eyes, it transforms into a massive skeletal beast, dragging its torso along the ground.
Alonsa tries to brace for impact.
*I just came back to life, I can't die again!!!*

Her body shatters as it hits the ground. She remains conscious as she witnesses pieces of herself fly in every direction, scattering around her point of impact. Her head remains intact, allowing her to witness this strange sight. Not a single drop of blood is spilled. No organs are splattered about. Her lower body has simply broken up into fine particles. Sand.
"Wh.. what?"
"I'm alive?"
Alonsa doesn't... feel like they just feel down many feet. If there is a pain, its dull and muted.
They try to lift their hand, even knowing that its scattered somewhere around the enviornment.

She can feel every piece of her hand, individually attempting to lift itself. The grains begin to roll together, attempting to compose itself back into a recognizable shape. The process is slow, and the beast is approaching. If she continues to lie in its path, she will be crushed under its dragging ribcage.
"Shit!!!"
Alonsa tries as hard as they can to move while their body reassembles itself.

The muscles in her neck, or whatever facsimile of those muscles exists, don't allow her to get very far. A voice speaks from behind her, its owner crawling into her limited range of view.

"Virchow...?"
"No, we can't let him! We need to stop him somehow!"
"He's gonna destroy everything!"

A guttural noise rises from Virchow's throat. It travels through his long neck, and reaches his mouth, accompanied by a spray of blood. Another follows in turn, then several more. He laughs, and laughs and laughs. His throat sounds as if it will be torn apart by the force of his own guffaw, but he cannot help himself. If his tear ducts hadn't been sealed shut by his hastily melded together body, he would be crying tears of joy.
Alonsa tries harder to move their body.
"I don't even get it. Isn't this the opposite of everything you wanted!?"

His laughter quiets down, and he turns to face Alonsa. With an elated voice, he responds. "Do you not see? My folly, it is as clear as the desert sky! I wished to cage a feral beast. Alonsa scrambles to put themselves together while Virchow rambles
"The gender of that thing... is the least of our worries right now! I think!"
"Maybe?"
"I mean I know it's like a symbol of the total depth of our lack of understanding of our own nature or something like that"
"But! It's also going to kill us!!"

"How can you not understand..." Virchow shakes his neck, and in turn, his head. "We have created this divine entity. It is the result of our beliefs... our faith. You and I... we shall be spared, do you not see? This is our reward... to be welcomed into the next world!"
"I don't follow!"
"But even if I did, I want it to spare everyone else too!!"

"This world has served its purpose. It had to remain, a physical reminder to cultivate our savior. But now, all that needs to remain... is our everlasting love." Virchow stares up at the beast, its towering skull casting a shadow over them. Alonsa's arm finishes reconstructing itself, fusing with her shoulder. Her torso and other limbs continue to roll together, piece by piece.
"We can do... better than that!" Alonsa strains to move their body.
"We're trying to make the world better!!"

She can move somewhat more with a complete arm, but it's not easy. The beast above stops crawling, only a short distance away from Alonsa and Virchow. It lowers its skull, facing them with hollow eyes. It seems to be examining them.
Alonsa looks up at it, and then nervously waves.

Its jaw opens, and what appears to be a tongue crawls forth. Its end reshapes, twisting and molding itself into a new form. The man's piercing orange eyes, their spiraling madness freed from its coiling prison, stare at the two on the ground.

"Father. Alonsa."
Alonsa can't respond. They just look, in awe and terror.

"My child... my Prince... you are everything I wished for, and more... please, accept my love. It is all I have to offer." Virchow raises his arms. Is it in pray, or for an embrace? It doesn't matter.

A second tongue emerges from the mouth. Its end transforms into the likeness of Thromb Cruor. A quiet fury rests on his face. "I was free to travel, under my new identity. To hunt, and live in peace and solitude. But I kept pulling myself back."

A third tongue. The likeness of the boy, from so long ago, appears on its end. He appears troubled, worried by something. "I didn't get it. Why did I keep coming back? What was it for? I didn't understand at all..."
"Thromb..."
Alonsa tries hard to reassemble themselves.
"I'm sorry, I... I don't know, I..."
"I wanted to help."

Her other arm reattaches, and her torso builds itself out. She's like the beast now, complete from the waste up. She can crawl in these blistering sands.

"I figured it out." "Alonsa, it's thanks to you." "I know why I came back." The three of them speak.
